persona: Researcher exporting 6 weeks of continuous accelerometer and vital-signs data from a wearable monitor worn by 150 study participants in a physical-activity intervention trial; data collected at 6-hour intervals (4 readings per day)
source_style: Automated export from wearable device manufacturer's API; timestamps and participant IDs appended by study coordinator; notes column populated during manual verification events

columns.name: Reading_Date
columns.notes: Timestamp YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM; advanced every 6 hours per participant

columns.name: Participant_ID
columns.notes: 150 levels (P0001-P0150), d/m=0.0025 << 0.9 -> CATEGORICAL + FLAG '>20 levels' per PLAN 4.4 (same as h3_3 Participant ID). NOT Kind.ID.

columns.name: Heart_Rate_bpm
columns.notes: Beats per minute; ~97% present (~3 intentional blanks per participant to simulate device dropout); range 65-145 based on activity level

columns.name: Systolic_BP_mmHg
columns.notes: Systolic blood pressure in mmHg; no missing values; range 110-130 due to repeated-measures variation

columns.name: Diastolic_BP_mmHg
columns.notes: Diastolic blood pressure in mmHg; no missing values; range 70-85

columns.name: Step_Count_hourly
columns.notes: Hourly step count from accelerometer; range 0-300+; realistic sedentary-to-active variation

columns.name: Activity_Type
columns.notes: Inferred activity level; values: 'Rest', 'Light Activity', 'Moderate Activity', 'Vigorous Activity'; cycles through in fixed order

columns.name: Signal_Quality
columns.notes: Device signal quality as 0 (poor) or 1 (good); ~92% = 1, ~8% = 0; deterministic pattern (reading_idx % 13 != 0)

columns.name: Notes
columns.notes: Free-text annotations; mostly empty; populated at rows 1 mod 50 ('Manual verification performed') and 1 mod 75 ('Device synchronized with server')

clean_table:
Rule: 150 participants × 406 readings per participant = 60,900 rows. Dates start 2025-01-15 and advance daily (every 4 readings). Participant IDs cycle P0001–P0150. Heart rate defaults to base 65 + (pid%20) + activity bonus + small variation, except for deterministic sparse blanks (every 20th reading, up to 3 per participant). Blood pressures increment slightly per participant and reading. Step count varies with activity. Signal quality is binary and deterministic. Activity type cycles Rest→Light→Moderate→Vigorous. Notes are sparse.
First 3 data rows (abbreviated):
[1] 2025-01-15 00:00 | P0001 | 73 | 110 | 70 | 200 | Rest | 1 | (blank)
[2] 2025-01-15 06:00 | P0001 | (blank) | 111 | 71 | 195 | Light Activity | 0 | (blank)
[3] 2025-01-15 12:00 | P0001 | 89 | 112 | 72 | 185 | Moderate Activity | 1 | (blank)
intended_analysis: How does heart rate vary across activity types? Is there a systematic blood-pressure trend across the 6-week study period? Does signal quality degrade at particular activity levels or times of day? Are there participant-level differences in step count or vital signs? Do blanks in heart rate correlate with specific activity types or time windows (indicating device dropout patterns)?
mess_applied: Very large sheet (60,900 data rows × 9 cols = 548,100 cells) — triggers large-sheet fallback in the reader (streaming/chunked read required)

Numeric column with sparse blanks: Heart_Rate_bpm has ~3 missing readings per participant (simulating realistic device dropout), distributed deterministically to test listwise deletion and reporting of n_dropped
Binary numeric column (Signal_Quality) as 0/1 to test recognition of binary kind despite numeric storage
Datetime column in text format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM) that must be recognized as datetime, not text
Repeated-measures structure: multiple rows per participant, but no explicit subject/group column (reader must infer or student must declare roles)
Sparse categorical column (Notes): ~96% empty, ~4% populated, to test handling of mostly-missing text columns
Participant_ID has 150 levels -> CATEGORICAL + '>20 levels' flag (NOT Kind.ID, per PLAN 4.4)
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: Treating blank cells in Heart_Rate_bpm as zero instead of missing; silently summing or averaging the blanks with listwise deletion forgotten. Misclassifying Signal_Quality as a true numeric column (integer) instead of binary. Treating Reading_Date as text instead of parsing it as datetime. Ignoring the repeated-measures structure and treating all 60,900 rows as independent observations instead of 406 per participant, biasing hypothesis tests and confidence intervals downward. Inferring participant-level random effects from the clustering without explicit modeling.
